newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy budget package worth 62.5 trln lire - official.
newsitem.headline: Italy budget package worth 62.5 trln lire - official.

text.p: The government's 1997 budget will cut a total 62.5 trillion lire off next year's public sector deficit, a statement from Prime Minister Romano Prodi's office said on Friday.
It said the heart of the package was worth 37.5 trillion lire, with 25 trillion lire coming from planned spending cuts and 12.5 trillion lire from fresh revenues.

In addition, the government intends to raise 13 trillion lire from a special "Euro Tax" and 12 trillion lire from so far unspecified "treasury operations." Both measures will be fully elaborated before the end of the year.
Among the spending cuts, the government aims to save 1.2 trillion lire from health spending and 6.1 trillion lire from pensions and welfare spending, the statement said.
A further 4.68 trillion lire will be cut from transfers to local and regional authorities and three trillion lire from transfers to the state railways and road maintenance group ANAS.

On the revenue front, the Treasury is looking for 3.31 trillion lire from a further crack down on tax evasion, 2.56 trillion lire from taxing fringe benefits and one trillion lire from national lotteries.
The statement added that 4.285 trillion lire of fresh revenues still had to be worked out, but would be announced by the end of the year.
The measures were approved after an 11 hour cabinet meeting on Friday. Further details would be released over the weekend, a government spokesman said.
